newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe sets jobs, EU, reform priorities for 97.
newsitem.headline: Juppe sets jobs, EU, reform priorities for 97.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Wednesday set his government three priorities for 1997: jobs, European Union commitments and more reforms.
Echoing a New Year message by President Jacques Chirac, the centre-right premier told a meeting of his ministers that "there will be no lack of difficulties in 1997."

"The president has said so twice -- France is certainly on the move, but at the same time we know that there is resistance in institutions. And we will come up against them in 1997 as in 1996," Juppe said, referring to protests and strikes in several sectors sparked by his austerity-driven reforms.

Juppe urged his team to stress three priorities this year. "First of all employment, that is our obsession...1997 is a decisive year (for Europe)," he said, adding that plans to set up a single European currency must succeed.
On reforms, he said: "The time for reforms is not behind us, it is ahead of us."

In his New Year address, Chirac pledged faster economic growth and lower taxes. His popularity and that of Juppe have slumped to record lows in the face of austerity policies, rising unemployment and labour conflicts.
Unemployment hit a record 12.7 percent in November, resuming its steady rise after a surprise drop in October, and economists said the peak was still some way off.
